newsitem.title: USA: US proposes oil spill financial responsiblity rule.
newsitem.headline: US proposes oil spill financial responsiblity rule.

text.p: The U.S. Minerals Management Service Tuesday issued its proposed rule to implement a new offshore oil spill financial responsibility law Congress passed last year to ease financial requirements for most offshore drilling operations.

The rule, which would cover the Outer Continental Shelf and state waters that are seaward of a line of ordinary low water, would apply to parties operating structures, equipment, pipelines and other devices used for oil exploration, drilling or production.

The proposal would ease blanket requirements that facilities show $150 million in financial responsibility, and instead would require demonstration of at least $35 million for facilities in the OCS and $10 million for facilities in state waters to cover liability and cleanup of a spill.
The proposal could require facilities to show up to $150 million in financial responsibility if the MMS believes it is warranted.
It generally exempts facilities with a worst case oil-spill discharge of 1,000 barrels or less, but there could be exceptions.
The MMS gave two options for defining the waters covered by this proposed rule.

The first option would include submerged coastal areas subject to tidal influence, which means the area could change with time in dynamic areas such as the Mississippi River Delta. This would not include large inland water bodies affected by tides or smaller landlocked water bodies along coasts.

The second option would include areas affected by the tides lying between the coastline and a parallel line that is a fixed distance from the coastline. The MMS said the band should be wide enough to cover prominent coastal bays and estuaries, and suggested it should be 50 to 100 miles wide.
The MMS said it will consider comments on the proposed rule received by June 23, and said it may "not fully consider" comments received after that time.
